title: The First Atmosphere Found on a Rocky World in the Habitable Zone
hook: For the first time, astronomers have caught a rocky planet in its star's habitable zone holding onto an atmosphere — spotted by the helium slowly bleeding off into space.
key_points: LHS 1140 b is the first rocky planet in a star's habitable zone confirmed to have an atmosphere.
The atmosphere revealed itself through helium slowly escaping into space from the planet's upper layers.
It was detected with the WINERED spectrograph at the Magellan Observatory in Chile.
The planet orbits a red dwarf about 48 light-years away, in the zone where liquid water could exist.
Astronomers estimate the atmosphere has survived more than three billion years — a good sign for long-term habitability.
content_html: Finding a rocky planet in the "habitable zone" — the orbital band where a world could hold liquid water — is exciting, but it's only half the story. Without an atmosphere, a rocky planet is just a bare, irradiated ball. Confirming that such a world actually keeps an atmosphere has been out of reach. Until now.
extra_html: Astronomers at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, with lead author Collin Cherubim and advisors Robin Wordsworth and David Charbonneau, reported the first confirmed atmosphere around a rocky planet in another star's habitable zone. The planet, LHS 1140 b, orbits a red dwarf about 48 light-years away. Rather than imaging the atmosphere directly, the team caught it leaking: helium slowly escaping into space, detected with the Warm Infrared Echelle (WINERED) spectrograph at the Magellan Observatory in Chile. From the escape signature, they estimate the atmosphere has persisted for more than three billion years — evidence that this world can cling to its air over the long haul, which is exactly what you'd want in a candidate for habitability. That makes LHS 1140 b one of the most promising targets yet in the search for life beyond Earth. Published in Science.

related.title: James Webb Reveals a Strange Atmosphere on a Hellish Lava Planet
related.hook: A planet so hot its surface is an ocean of molten rock turns out to have a real atmosphere — built from gases venting straight out of the lava itself, JWST finds.

related.title: We Might Already Be Overlooking Signs of Alien Life
related.hook: It's not just that we haven't found alien life — researchers warn we might be looking right at evidence of it and not recognizing it, because we mostly search for signs that look like Earth's own.

related.title: A Giant Planet Was Hiding in the Dust Around Beta Pictoris
related.hook: A giant planet sat hidden for years inside one of astronomy's most-studied systems — Webb found it not by seeing it, but by sniffing out its atmosphere through a veil of dust.

flashcards.prompt: What makes LHS 1140 b a milestone in the search for habitable worlds?
flashcards.back_html: It's the first rocky planet in a star's habitable zone confirmed to have an atmosphere — the zone where liquid water could exist on the surface.

flashcards.prompt: How did astronomers detect the planet's atmosphere?

choices.text: By observing helium slowly escaping into space from the planet's upper atmosphere
By photographing clouds directly on the planet's surface
By detecting radio signals emitted by the atmosphere

flashcards.explanation_html: Using the WINERED spectrograph at Chile's Magellan Observatory, the team saw helium leaking off the planet — the signature that revealed the atmosphere.

flashcards.prompt: Why does the atmosphere's estimated age matter?
flashcards.back_html: Astronomers think it has lasted more than three billion years. Surviving that long suggests the planet can hold an atmosphere over the timescales relevant to life.
